sections.html:
Pelham is a Shelby County city in the Birmingham metro area, about 20 miles south of downtown Birmingham and 72 miles north of Montgomery. It incorporated on July 10, 1964, covers about 39 square miles at roughly 830 feet of elevation, and uses ZIP code 35124.

Oak Mountain State Park, the largest state park in Alabama, lies within the city, so many house hunters arrive for the trails and lakes as much as for the homes. That is worth a line in any listing.

Most of that growth happened within two decades of incorporation. The 2020 census counted 9,777 housing units with only 2.9 percent vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.7 percent and the rental rate was 5.1 percent, so very little housing sits empty.

Because so much of Pelham was built after 1980, much of its housing is a few decades old. Inspectors on houses of that age commonly look at roof coverings and flashing, heating and air systems, water heaters and original windows. Shelby County as a whole is 78.1 percent owner-occupied, so most of your competition on a listing is other owners, not rentals.

US Route 31 runs straight through Pelham, and Interstate 65 reaches the city at exits 242 and 246. ClasTran provides weekday dial-a-ride service, and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport is in the next county over. US 231 and US 280 also cross Shelby County.

Many residents commute north into Birmingham, and others work locally. Give buyers the real distance to the interstate and to Birmingham when you describe the house, because commute length drives much of the conversation in a suburb like this.

Pelham City Schools has run the city's public schools since July 1, 2014, when it split from the Shelby County system. It has two elementary schools, one middle school and Pelham High School. Before the split, some parts of Pelham beside Chelsea attended Chelsea schools. Houses in that part of town can still prompt boundary questions, so check assignments by address before quoting them.

Private options in the county include Briarwood Christian School and Westminster School at Oak Mountain. Jefferson State's Shelby-Hoover campus and the University of Montevallo are within reach.

Shelby County has about 223,000 residents, ranks sixth in Alabama by population and has its seat in Columbiana. Its 2020 population was 223,024 and a 2025 estimate is 238,552. Growth came from the interstate and US 31 and spread across Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea. A Pelham seller therefore competes with houses in several nearby cities, each with its own school district.

Farmland, rail and later the interstate built the county. It was founded on February 7, 1818, and went from 38,037 people in 1970 to 66,298 in 1980. The first county seat, Shelbyville, stood in what is now Pelham beginning in 1820, before the seat moved to Columbiana in 1826.

The southern end of the Appalachians crosses Shelby County, with Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain, while other parts are flat. Water drains mainly to the Cahaba and Coosa rivers.

A house on a slope may bring drainage, retaining wall and foundation questions. A house near a creek bed deserves a closer look at the flood zone. Learn the answers before a buyer asks, since an unexplained crack or a damp crawl space is the kind of thing that cuts an offer.

Pelham runs under the Mayor and Council Act, with the mayor as chief executive. The city has its own building inspector, permits clerk, revenue department, waterworks and city clerk, and several of them touch a house sale. The building inspector and permits clerk handle work done without paperwork, waterworks handles utility accounts and the revenue department handles local licenses.

If a prior owner finished a basement or added a room, ask the city whether a permit was pulled before you list. A missing permit can slow a financed sale, though it is less of a barrier for a buyer who purchases as is.

Alabama Code section 40-22-1 puts a recordation tax of 50 cents on each $500 of value in a deed. The probate judge collects it before recording, and a recording fee is separate.

Property taxes come due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. The Shelby County offices in Columbiana hold the parcel records and can supply a payoff figure. Ask for it early so the closing statement is accurate.

sections.h2: If you owe a mortgage or back taxes
sections.html:
A balance on the house does not stop a sale. The title company gets a payoff letter from your lender and a tax figure from the county, then pays both at closing out of your proceeds. You receive what is left.

Back taxes, liens and unpaid utility bills show up in the title search, and each is settled at the same table. Request the search early so you can see the full list and decide whether the offer still makes sense once everything is paid. Ask the closer to walk you through each line on the settlement statement before you sign.

If you are behind on the mortgage, tell the buyer. A firm closing date can matter more than a higher number when a lender is waiting, and a cash buyer can often move on a schedule that a financed sale cannot match.

A cash sale is worth a look when you want a firm date and no repairs. Pelham examples:

  • A house from the years of fast growth that needs a roof and a new air system before it would pass a buyer's inspection.
  • An estate property the heirs do not want to maintain.
  • An owner moving for work who cannot wait out a long listing period.

The path is short. You describe the house and we make an offer. If you accept, a title company researches ownership, orders any payoffs and sets the closing date. You sign, the lender and tax bill are paid from the proceeds, and the rest goes to you.

Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays closing costs and read the contract before you sign. Compare the offer to the likely net from a listing after repairs, fees and the carrying cost of the months a house may sit. We buy Pelham houses as they are and you are free to decline.

Bring a photo ID, the deed, the latest tax bill and your lender's payoff information to the closing. If the house is part of an estate, bring the paperwork showing who may sign. Ask whether the buyer's offer depends on a loan or an inspection, and ask what happens to your deposit if the sale falls through.

Make a note of what is staying and what is going. Appliances, window coverings and fixtures should be listed in the contract so nobody argues about them at the walkthrough. Turn off or transfer utilities only after the closing date is firm.

faqs.a: Pelham is in Shelby County, in the Birmingham metro area.

faqs.q: How far is Pelham from Birmingham?
faqs.a: Downtown Birmingham is about 20 miles north, reached by US 31 or Interstate 65.

faqs.q: When are Pelham property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Does Pelham have its own school system?
faqs.a: Yes. Pelham City Schools began on July 1, 2014 and runs two elementary schools, a middle school and Pelham High School.
